items.title: Harrison Verrett Interview, 1961-08-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Someone was, I don't know whether it was Ken Mills, someone was saying something about your brother.

ctx.x: I never heard from Percy, it's been way back in 1936, and I haven't heard from Percy Severe since. There were a couple of musicians that have left here that killed D and stood here. And Cyril August, he was a, him and Cyril August and this guy here, oh, I can't think of him, he's still going strong on the alto horn, he plays a lot of alto, he makes a lot of recordings. Earl Bostic. Well, they was two top men's here during them times, Cyril August and Earl Bostic. Earl was working at the La Vida and Cyril was at…

Someone was, I don't know whether it was Ken Mills, someone was saying something about your brother. Did you have a brother that also played a musical instrument? Well I have a brother but he don't play dance music, he only plays, he's 70 in Venice,

he's next to me. He plays saxophone, clarinet, but he plays in church. Oh I see. He never did play dance music. But I have a first cousin he played, Samuel Lee, he played with practically all of them. Known beds in the city, he had Faye Marble, Pichon, Sidney Desveen, P-Rone, Joe Robichaud, huh? Is he still in town? No, he's in Los Angeles. No, he's in Los Angeles, he moved to Los Angeles. Does he have a pen for it? Samuel Lee, they call him Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland They…
